sentences.text: JUDGMENT

This judgment is emerged consequent upon the petition filed by the petitioners U/S 166 of M.V. Act,
claiming compensation of Rs.70,00,000/- on account of the death of Hemanth Kumar M, in a road traffic accident.

2. The case of the petitioners, in brief, is as follows:
On 08-12-2023 at about 3.40 p.m., the deceased was proceeding on his motorcycle bearing No. KA-01-HE-9391 on the left side of the road near Nagarabhiruddhi Bhavan, Old Madras road, Bangalore at that time, the driver of the bus bearing No.
KA-51-AJ-2306 came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the scooter of the deceased and caused the accident.
Due to the impact, the deceased fell down and sustained grievous injuries and died on the spot.
The petitioners have spent Rs.3,00,000/- towards funeral, obsequies and other incidental charges.

Prior to the accident, deceased was hale and healthy, aged about 33 years and working as interior decorator and earning Rs.30,000/ per month and he was contributing his entire income for the maintenance of his family.
Due to the untimely death of deceased the petitioners have suffered mentally and physically, they have lost their bread earner.
The petitioners were the parents and sister of the deceased Hemanth Kumar M. have lost their love and affection towards their son and brother.
The respondent No.1 & 2 are the owner and insurer of the offending bus are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
Accordingly, prays to award compensation of Rs.70,00,000/- with interest to the petitioners.
3. After service of notices, respondent No.1 owner remained absent and placed exparte.

The Respondent No.2 insurance company appeared through its counsel and filed written statement by admitting the issuance of insurance policy in respect of the bus bearing no. KA-51-AJ-2306 and the liability of this respondent, if any, is subject to terms and conditions of the policy. Further denied the cause and manner of accident and also further contended that at the time of accident the driver of the offending bus was not holding valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident.
Further this respondent has denied the age, occupation and income of the deceased.
The compensation claimed by the petitioners is exorbitant and fanciful.
Hence the respondent No.2 prays to dismiss the petition against it.

4. On the basis of the rival contentions, the following issues were framed by this court:
ISSUES

1 . Whether the petitioners prove that deceased Hemanth Kumar M. died in the motor vehicle accident that occurred on 08-12-2023 at about 3.40 p.m. near Nagarabhiruddhi Bhavan, OM Road, Bangalore due to the rash and negligence driving of the bus bearing Reg. No. KA-51-AJ-2306 by its driver?
2. Whether the petitioners prove that they are the legal heirs and dependents of deceased?
3. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, what amount and from whom?
4 . What order or award?
5. In order to prove the claim petition, the 2 nd petitioner is examined as PW.1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.13.
The second respondent examined its official as RW.1 and got marked one document at Ex.R1.

6. Heard the arguments and perused the material evidence that is available on record.
7. My findings on the above issues are as under.
 Issue No.1 : In the affirmative,
 Issue No.2 : In the affirmative,
 Issue No.3 : In the affirmative
Issue No.4 : As per final orders
for the following.-

REASONS ISSUE NO.1:
8.

The petitioners to prove their claim have produced true copies of FIR, complaint,
spot mahazar along with sketch, IMV report, inquest report, PM report and head of charge sheet, which are marked under Ex.P.1 to 8.
9.
As per the documents, Ex.P1 FIR is came to be registered on the basis of the complaint given by petitioner No.1 as per Ex.P2.
In the Ex.P2, they have alleged the rash and negligent driving by the driver of bus bearing No. KA-51-AJ-2306.
After the registration of FIR the IO conducted the spot mahazar and IMV report.
As per the spot mahazar marked at Ex.P3 and rough sketch marked at Ex.P4 the accident spot is in the left side of the road.

sentences.text: The accident spot is within 8 feet of the left side edge of the road.
The Ex.P5 is the IMV report wherein the bus bearing No. KA-51-AJ-2306 has got damaged in its front left side bumper and left side center running body.
In the same way the motor cycle of the deceased has got damaged in its right side also.

Keeping these contents of mahazar and IMV report in back ground, in the complaint itself it is alleged that the driver of bus bearing No. KA- 51-AJ-2306 by driving his bus in a rash and negligent manner dashed against the right side of the motor cycle of the deceased.

As such the mahazar and rough sketch establishes that the driver of bus bearing No. KA-51-AJ-2306 changed his lane towards left side, as such it got damages in the front left side bumper and left side center running body.

10. The contents of mahazar, rough sketch and IMV report marked at Ex.P3,P4 & P5 establishes that the driver of bus bearing No. KA-51-AJ-2306 has changed his lane from the middle road to left side,
thereby the bus dashed against the right side of the motor cycle of deceased.
If the driver of bus bearing No. KA-51-AJ-2306 has not changed the lane and if he has changed the lane after giving prior indications the said accident is not going to be caused.
The damages mentioned in Ex.P5 reveals that the changing of the lane by the driver of bus bearing No. KA-51-AJ-2306 is the sole reason for the accident.

11. The respondent No.1 owner neither filed written statement nor examined its driver to show that with all precautions and with giving prior indication the driver of bus bearing No. KA-51-AJ-2306 has changed the lane.
No such efforts are made by the respondent No.1 - owner.

The contents of mahazar, rough sketch and IMV report marked at Ex.P3,P4 & P5 establishes the negligence of the driver of bus bearing No. KA-51-AJ-2306.
12.
Ex.P7 is the postmortem report and Ex.P6 is the inquest.
where both these documents discloses that the deceased succumbed due to the injuries sustained by him in the said accident.

13. The respondent No.2 - insurance company examined it sofficia has RW.1 by denying the negligence of the driver of bus bearing No. KA-51-AJ-2306, but as admitted by the RW.1 he has no personal knowledge about the accident and his evidence is based on the documents.
Whereas the documents reveals the negligence of the driver of bus bearing No. KA-51-AJ-2306.

Further the RW.1 even though denied the contents of rough sketch no other independent evidence is placed to hold the contrary opinion to the opinion of the IO as per the charge sheet marked at Ex.P8.
14.

It is necessary to reassert that in a claim for compensation filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is expected to prove the incident on basis of principle of preponderance of probabilities and the view taken by this Court is fortified by the decision rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others which is reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319.

entities.text: Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530 has observed that, it is necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.

entities.text: Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The claimants are merely required to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied.

Further the Hon'ble High Court of Jayalakshmi vs Infants Travels Pvt Ltd on 7 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/39090045/
4

Karnataka in National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Krishnappa and another reported in 2001 ACJ 1105,
where the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka considering the fact that the rider of the offending vehicle was not examined to prove any contributory negligence on the part of scooterist held that the accident had occurred due to rash or negligent driving by the rider of the offending van.

sentences.text: 15. Even here in this case the driver of the offending bus bearing No. KA-51-AJ-2306 is not examined to show that there was no negligence on his part and even otherwise the IO, in the charge sheet as already observed, and clearly opined that the accident occurred only due to the fault of the driver of the offending bus bearing No. KA-51-AJ-2306 and he was charge sheeted.

16. In view of the ratio laid down in the authorities referred to above and applying the settled principle of law to the case at hand, which is further supported by the oral and documentary evidence adduced by PW-1, this Tribunal is of the considered opinion that the accident leading to this case indeed occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of offending bus bearing No.KA-51-AJ-2306 resulting in deceased sustaining injuries.

17. The injury sustained by the deceased is mentioned in Ex.P6 inquest and Ex.P7 postmortem,
which also evidentiates the nature of the accident and injuries sustained by the deceased.
Ex.P8 is the charge sheet filed against the driver of the offending bus bearing No. KA-51-AJ-2306 for the offence punishable under Sec. 279 & 304 (A) of IPC.
The investigating officer as per Ex.P8 charge sheet opined that the driver of offending bus bearing No. KA-51-AJ-2306 driven the said vehicle in a rash and negligent manner.
No other evidence is placed by the respondents to show the contributory negligence by the deceased.
During the course of cross-examination of PW.1, nothing has been elicited so as to disprove the case of the petitioners.
18. As per well settled position of law the standard of proof in claim petition like present one, is only preponderance of probabilities.

Looking to the oral as well as documentary evidence of the petitioners there are sufficient materials to show that Hemanth Kumar M died in the accident dated 08-12-2023 which is caused by the driver of the bus bearing No.KA-51-AJ-2306.
Accordingly issue No.1 answered in the affirmative.
ISSUE NO.2 19.

As held herein above, the petitioners have proved that Hemanth Kumar M died on 08-12-2023 due to the injuries sustained in RTA, which is caused by respondent No.1.
20.
As contended in the petition the petitioners are the parents and sister of the deceased Hemanth Kumar M.
The respondents do not specifically deny the relationship of petitioners with deceased.
The petitioners to prove their relationship with the deceased, have produced the notarized copies of Aadhar cards of petitioners along with deceased which are marked under Ex.P12 & 13.
During the course of recording the evidence the notarized copies of Aadhar cards are compared with the original documents and found correct.
The respondents do not dispute the Aadhar cards produced by the petitioners.
The respondent No.2 has not adduced any evidence to disprove the relationship of the petitioners with the deceased.

sentences.text: In the absence of contradictory evidence the evidence of the petitioner is to be accepted and it is considered that, petitioners are the parents and unmarried sister of deceased being the dependents are entitled for compensation.
Accordingly Issue No.2 is answered in the Affirmative.

Issue No.3 :
22.

The issued No.1 & 2 are answered in the affirmative by holding that the deceased Hemanth Kumar died in the Rta dated 08-12-2023 caused by the negligence driving by the driver of bus bearing No. KA-51-AJ-2306 and the petitioners are entitled for the compensation.
23. Now the quantum of compensation is to be decided.
In the Aadhaar card and driving license of the deceased Hemanth Kumar are produced at Ex.P12, the date of birth of the deceased is shown as 12.1.1990.
If it is considered, as on the date of the accident the age of the deceased was 33 years.

24. As stated in the petition deceased was working as interior decorator and earning Rs.30,000/-
per month.
To prove the said fact, the petitioners have produced income tax returns and its annexures and account statement as per Ex.P9 & 10.
On perusal of Ex.P10 account statement it shows that the payments received by the deceased through online.
Further the Ex.P9 being the income tax returns of the assessment year 2020-2021 the declared income was Rs.4,28,240/-.
The said Ex.P9 income tax returns was electronically submitted on 31- 03-2021 ie., much before 2 years of the accident.
In the said Ex.P9 Rs.1,000/- was paid as tax by the deceased.
As such by deducting the said tax amount of Rs.1,000/- and rounding off the same Rs..4,27,000/- is considered as the annual income of the deceased.
25. As per Sarala varma's case the proper multiplier applicable to the age of deceased is 16.

Since the deceased is a bachelor 50% of the income is to be deducted towards his personal expenses, then the total loss of dependency would be Rs.34,16,000/- (Rs.4,27,000/- X 16 = Rs.68,32,000/- minus half of the income i.e., (68,32,000 - 34,16,000) = Rs.34,16,000/-).

26. In Civil Special leave petition (Civil No.25590/2014 dated 31.10.2016 (National Insurance Company Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi & others), the Hon'ble Supreme Court has held that "While determining the income, in case the deceased was self- employed or on a fixed salary, an addition of 40% of the established income should be the warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 years.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi & others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: An addition of 25% where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years and 10% where the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.
The established income means the income minus the tax component."
27. As per the above decisions 40% out of loss of dependency has to be granted towards future prospects which would Rs.13,66,400/-.

28. LOSS OF CONSORTIUM:
In Magma General Insurance company Limited Vs. Nanuram (2018) 18 SCC 130, the Hon'ble Apex court has observed "Consortium" is a compendious term, which Jayalakshmi vs Infants Travels Pvt Ltd on 7 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/39090045/
6 encompasses spousal consortium, parental consortium and filial consortium.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The right to consortium would include the company, care, help, comfort, guidance, solace and affection of the deceased, which is a loss to his family.

With respect to a spouse, it would include sexual relations with the deceased spouse".
29.
The Petitioners are the Parents and unmarried sister of the deceased and they have lost their loving son and brother.
Therefore they are entitled to a sum of Rs.44,000/-(Rs.40,000/x 10% hike every three years from 2017 as per Pranay Sethi Case) under the head of loss of consortium.

30. Further I inclined to award Rs.50,000/- towards loss of love and affection, Rs.16,500/- towards loss of estate and Rs.16,500/- towards funeral expenses (this amount is calculated as per Pranaya Sethi case with enhanced rate at 10% after three years).

The petitioners are entitled for compensation under the following heads:
1. Loss of dependency Rs. 34,16,000/-
2. Loss of future prospects Rs. 13,66,400/-
3. Loss of consortium Rs. 44,000/-
4. Love and affection Rs. 50,000/-
5. Funeral expenses Rs. 16,500/-
6. Transport of dead body Rs. 16,500/-
Total Rs
31. Liability:-
In the petition it is alleged that the respondent No.1& 2 are the owner and insurer of the bus bearing No. KA-51-AJ-2306.
The respondent No.2 in its written statement has admitted the issuance of policy to the offending vehicle.
No other offences are invoked against the driver of the bus for driving the offending bus bearing No.KA-51-AJ-2306 without valid insurance policy.
No other grounds are made out to show the violation of policy conditions by respondent No.1 owner.
As discussed above, the petitioners successfully proved the negligence on the part of the driver of bus bearing No. KA-51-AJ-2306.
Thereby, the respondent No.1 & 2 being the owner and insurer are liable to pay the compensation along with the interest.

Hence, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner and the respondent No.2 insurance company shall indemnify the compensation on behalf of the respondent No.1.
32.

In the judgment of the Hon'ble high court of Karnataka in M.F.A. no.8625 of 2023 (MV-D)
between The Oriental Insurance Company Ltd v/s. Sri. Gummanna and others wherein it is held as Jayalakshmi vs Infants Travels Pvt Ltd on 7 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/39090045/

22.One of the grounds urged by respondent No.1 is that although petitioners are entitled for interest on the compensation granted from the date of petition till realization, no interest is to be allowed on the portion of the compensation granted under the head loss of future prospects, as there would be no delay in payment of the same and since it would become due at a point of time which has not yet arisen.

Seema Devi and 6 Ors In this decision, placing reliance on the decisions in Khusboo Chirania @ Kanta Chirania Vs Kamal Kumar Sovasaria (Khusboo), National Insurance Company Ltd Vs. Mst. Aisha Bano and Ors dated 14.07.2023 (Aisha Bano) and Smt.
Kalpana Madhu Gavali and Ors Vs Maharashtra State Road Transport Corporation dated 21.09.2023 (Kalpana), it was held that the compensation granted under the head loss of future prospects should not have been subjected to payment of any interest.

sentences.text: 19.2 In Aisha Bano, it was held that future prospects is relatable to an income to be received in the future and as such there could not be any loss to the claimants for the payment of future prospects at the time the deceased met with the accident.

The reason for awarding interest on the compensation amount minus the future prospects is due to the fact that though the loss of dependency starts from the date of the accident, the compensation amount is computed on the date of award of the Tribunal.

Interest is awarded to compensate the loss of money value on account of lapse of time,
such as the time taken for the legal proceedings and for the denial of right to utilise the money when due.

However, future prospects is with regard to probable income to be received in the future and as such there is no requirement to grant interest on the amount awardable towards future prospects, as the future is yet to happen.
Further, future prospects is given for the entire future and as such, the claimant is getting compensation in the lump sum prior to the occurrence of future events.
19.3 We are in the complete agreement with the above decisions.
Since the amount due under the head loss of future prospects is yet to become due, it would be illogical and illegal to direct the insurance company to pay interest on loss of future prospects.
Therefore, out of the total compensation payable, the respondent No.1 is not liable to pay any interest on the compensation under the head loss of future prospects.
However, so far as the remaining compensation, respondent No.1 is liable to pay interest at the rate of 6% p.a as directed by the Tribunal.
23.Thus
, the petitioners are entitled for interest at the rate of 6% p.a. on the enhanced compensation, except on Rs.6,04,800/- granted under the head loss of future prospects.
In the result appeal filed by respondent No.1 succeeds and accordingly, the following".
The compensation awarded in the head of future prospects is an income to be received in the future and as such there is no requirement to grant interest on the amount awarded under this head.

The future income is going to be received by the petitioners in one lump sum hence, by applying the above said precedent the petitioners are entitled for the interest at 6% per annum except on the amount awarded under the head of future prospects.

Accordingly, this issue answered in the Jayalakshmi vs Infants Travels Pvt Ltd on 7 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/39090045/

ISSUE NO.4:-
33.

For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioners U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioners are entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.49,09,400/- (Rupees Forty nine lakhs nine thousand and four hundred only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,. from the date of petition till the realization from respondents.
The respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order.
Out of the compensation amount, the petitioner No.1 to 3 are entitled for the compensation at the ratio of 40:30:30.
Further clarified that the compensation awarded under the head of future prospectus doesn't carries any interest.

Out of total compensation awarded to the Petitioner No.1 to 3, 50% shall be released in favour petitioner No.1 to 3 on their proper identification and remaining 50% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any Scheduled Bank, for a period of three years, in their names.
Advocate fee is fixed at 1,500/-.
Draw the award accordingly.

1 . Whether the petitioners prove that deceased Hemanth Kumar M. died in the motor vehicle accident that occurred on 08-12-2023 at about 3.40 p.m. near Nagarabhiruddhi Bhavan, OM Road, Bangalore due to the rash and negligence driving of the bus bearing Reg. No. KA-51-AJ-2306 by its driver?
2. Whether the petitioners prove that they are the legal heirs and dependents of deceased?
3. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, what amount and from whom?

22.One of the grounds urged by respondent No.1 is that although petitioners are entitled for interest on the compensation granted from the date of petition till realization, no interest is to be allowed on the portion of the compensation granted under the head loss of future prospects, as there would be no delay in payment of the same and since it would become due at a point of time which has not yet arisen.
However, future prospects is with regard to probable income to be received in the future and as such there is no requirement to grant interest on the amount awardable towards future prospects, as the future is yet to happen.
Further, future prospects is given for the entire future and as such, the claimant is getting compensation in the lump sum prior to the occurrence of future events.
Since the amount due under the head loss of future prospects is yet to become due, it would be illogical and illegal to direct the insurance company to pay interest on loss of future prospects.
Therefore, out of the total compensation payable, the respondent No.1 is not liable to pay any interest on the compensation under the head loss of future prospects.

In the result appeal filed by respondent No.1 succeeds and accordingly, the following".
The compensation awarded in the head of future prospects is an income to be received in the future and as such there is no requirement to grant interest on the amount awarded under this head.
The future income is going to be received by the petitioners in one lump sum hence, by applying the above said precedent the petitioners are entitled for the interest at 6% per annum except on the amount awarded under the head of future prospects.

The petitioners are entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.49,09,400/- (Rupees Forty nine lakhs nine thousand and four hundred only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,. from the date of petition till the realization from respondents.
